translationRepairs: the Banner Service Office was subordinate to it.
the Constables Office was subordinate to it.
番役處 is the office of constables and runners, not a banner service office.
At the time former Ming officials and temple officials were still employed side by side.
At the time former Ming officials and eunuchs were still employed side by side.
寺臣 here means palace eunuchs (寺人), not temple officials.
They were appointed by examination from juren, tribute students, and Supervising Students drawn from the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Chinese Brigade of the Eight Banners.
They were appointed by examination from juren, tribute students, and Imperial Academy students drawn from the Manchu, Mongol, and Han Chinese Brigade of the Eight Banners.
監 here is 監生, students of the Imperial Academy, not supervising students.
In the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign, following the precedent of the left and right divisions, bureau secretaries were ordered to have bodyguards concurrently administer the divisions.
In the sixth year of the Jiaqing reign, following the precedent of the left and right divisions, the hall-level duties were ordered to be concurrently handled by bodyguards.
堂上令侍衛兼司 means the hall-level duties were to be handled concurrently by bodyguards; no secretaries are mentioned.
Princes of the First Rank, Princes of the Second Rank, State Princesses, and Heir Princesses all had fixed regulations.
Princes of the First Rank, Princes of the Second Rank, State Princesses, and Heshuo Princesses all had fixed regulations.
和碩公主 are Heshuo (second-grade) princesses, not heir princesses.
In the seventh year of the Qianlong reign, regulations were set so that eunuchs receiving noble titles would not overstep their bounds.
In the seventh year of the Qianlong reign, regulations were set so that eunuchs receiving official ranks would not overstep their bounds.
受爵 here refers to eunuch official ranks (cf. next unit: not above rank 4), not noble titles.
